en: The Chapter on Similes, Part One: The Lion Section
3. The Question on the Peṇāhikā Bird “Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that ‘two qualities of the peṇāhikā bird should be adopted’—which are those two qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the peṇāhikā bird, out of jealousy toward her own husband, does not nourish her chicks;”

In the same way, Great King, when defilements have arisen in one who is practicing yoga, the practitioner of yoga should feel resentment toward them; having placed them within the well-secured opening of right restraint by means of the foundations of mindfulness, he should develop mindfulness directed to the body at the door of the mind.
This, Great King, is the first quality to be taken from the peṇāhikā bird.
Furthermore, Great King, after the peṇāhikā has spent the day searching for food in the forest, it approaches the flock of birds in the evening for its own protection.
In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga should dwell alone in solitude for the sake of liberation from the fetters.
Failing to find delight therein, he should enter the Saṅgha and live protected by the Saṅgha, in order to guard against the fear of reproach.
This, Great King, is the second quality to be adopted from the female snake.
This was also said, Great King, by Brahmā Sahampati in the presence of the Blessed One:
one should wander for the sake of liberation from the fetters.”
“If one does not find delight there,
one should dwell in the Saṅgha, guarding oneself and mindful.
Thus ends the third question on the peacock’s leg.
